findings: Six-dimension HANNA macro Spearman near zero is not rescued by overlap subsets or alternative aggregations, so the failure is unlikely to be a mapping or pooling artifact; residual signal is probably destroyed before scoring is combined.

The remaining failure modes that can zero rank correlation while leaving a broad HBQ bank intact are measurement-process errors: question wording vs HANNA construct text, item selection into the overlap set, batching/halo, polarity/scale direction, judge-prompt framing vs HANNA protocol, and exact-quote grounding errors.
Non-overlapping HBQ items are out of scope for HANNA alignment and must stay in the bank; they should be scored and stored but excluded from HANNA correlation, not pruned to manufacture overlap.
Holdout stories must remain untouched for confirmation only. Any threshold, mapping, wording change, or stop decision belongs on a locked development-story partition.
recommendations: Lock a development/validation story split first. Pre-register the HANNA-overlap item map, polarity signs, batch layout, and judge prompt on development stories only. Do not retune mappings, weights, wording, or stop thresholds after seeing validation.

On development stories only, run a sparse diagnostic in this order and change at most one class per cycle: (1) exact-quote/evidence failures, (2) polarity and scale direction, (3) prompt framing vs HANNA annotation protocol, (4) question wording against HANNA dimension definitions, (5) overlap item selection, (6) batching/order/halo. Re-score only the overlap slice after each cycle; leave non-overlap HBQ items untouched.

Exact-quote pass: for each overlap item, require the judge to return quote/span or explicit none. Flag invented quotes, wrong-character quotes, and questions that demand a quote the story cannot support. Repair by tightening evidence rules or rewriting the question so it does not require a nonexistent span.

Polarity pass: inventory reverse-keyed items, mixed Likert anchors, and double negatives. Recode signs on development labels before any aggregation. A few inverted items can cancel dimension ranks even when raw judgments are informative.

Framing pass: align judge instructions with HANNA (unit of evaluation, absolute vs relative quality, dimension definitions, disallowed extras such as style-guide or toxicity overlays). Keep the same framing for overlap and non-overlap items so coverage is not silently rewritten.

Wording/selection pass: pairwise-diff each overlap question against its HANNA dimension text. Drop or reword only items whose construct is not HANNA’s, is double-barreled, or is story-external. Do not add HANNA-paraphrase items that shrink remaining HBQ coverage. Batching pass: test isolated vs bundled overlap questions for halo and recency; prefer small same-construct batches or single-item calls if bundled ranks collapse.
Validation: freeze the repaired overlap scorer and evaluate once on untouched stories at dimension-level Spearman plus macro. Report non-overlap HBQ separately as coverage, never as a HANNA target.

Sparse priorities: quote integrity and polarity first; framing second; wording/selection third; batching last. Stop if development overlap Spearman remains indistinguishable from zero after quote+polarity+framing fixes. Stop if one wording/selection cycle plus one batching cycle does not move development Spearman beyond a pre-registered floor. Stop at the first cycle that clears the floor without using validation. Do not iterate on holdout, do not weight-search, and do not delete non-overlap HBQ to chase HANNA.
risks: Treating aggregation/overlap views as the next lever will overfit a mapping while the judge still hallucinates quotes, flips polarity, or scores a different construct than HANNA.
Rewriting overlap items toward HANNA language can quietly convert the bank into a HANNA clone and shrink genuine HBQ coverage even if item count is unchanged.
Repeated look at validation, or any holdout-driven wording/weight search, will manufacture alignment that will not replicate.
Batching changes can trade halo for instability; single-item scoring raises cost and may still fail if the prompt construct is wrong.
If quote+polarity+framing already fail on development, further wording work is likely construct mismatch, not a repairable rubric bug.
output.summary: HANNA alignment is failing before aggregation: keep full HBQ coverage, diagnose quote, polarity, framing, wording, selection, and batching on development stories only, then freeze and test once on untouched stories with sparse stops.
